title: I've been building a desktop investigation game
author: Kandoo85
selftext:
Been working on this for the last few weeks and thought I'd finally show some of it here.

It's called **ECHO//STATE: ERASURE**. The basic idea is a desktop investigation game where most of what you do happens inside this fictional operating system. You go through mails, messages, files, photos, videos, browser stuff, contacts etc. and piece things together from there.

This is very much still WIP though.

Especially a lot of the videos, images and smaller assets you see here are placeholders right now. Some will probably stay in some form, others will be replaced completely. I'm also not really happy with the look of every app yet, so there will definitely be another visual pass over a lot of this.

What I'm pretty happy about at the moment is that the whole thing finally runs stable. The desktop, the apps, navigation between everything and most of the basic systems are working now without me breaking something every five minutes :D

I'm getting close to 1,000 assets already, which sounds a bit stupid considering I haven't even finished Day 1 yet.

That includes everything though. Icons, UI stuff, documents, audio, images, videos, variations, random little things sitting somewhere in the OS...it adds up ridiculously fast.

I've been using quite a few different tools for it. Codex for a lot of the Unreal work, Nano Banana, GPT Image and Juggernaut for image assets, ElevenLabs for voices, MiniMax, Seedance and Omni Flash for video and Suno for some of the music.

Not everything generated actually makes it into the game either. There's been a lot of making something, putting it in, looking at it for five minutes and going "nah, that looks like shit" and replacing it again :D

Right now I mostly want to finish the desktop and all the apps properly. Once that's done, the basic framework of the game is there and I can build the rest of the story around it instead of constantly working on the foundation.

Still a lot to do, but it's moving in the right direction and I'm having way more fun with this than I expected.

I'm hoping I can have something like a playable **Day 1 demo** ready in a few weeks.

Anyway...this is the current state of it. If you got any questions about the process, feel free to ask :)

comments.author: Wooden_Plant7504
comments.body:
Hey. This looks good. It makes me think of the movies “searching” and “missing”.   
Could you elaborate a bit on your workflow with AI assisted dev/asset production if you are happy to share. How much do you use Codex, GPT images and elevenlabs ? Do you feel this accelerates you significantly ? Which parts are, in your view worth the subscription money.

replies.author: Kandoo85
replies.body:
Thanks :) Searching was definitely somewhere in the back of my head with this. Haven't seen Missing yet though, so I guess that's on the list now :D

Codex is probably the tool I use the most by quite a margin. I usually give it a fairly concrete task, let it work on the project, then I check the result in Unreal and go back with whatever I want changed. Sometimes that's functionality, sometimes it's literally "this looks terrible, redo it" :D

I'm not sitting there writing much code myself. Most of my time is spent deciding what I actually want, checking what it built and pushing it in the right direction. For me that works surprisingly well.

GPT Image and Nano Banana are much more situational. I use them when I need a specific asset, but I jump around a lot depending on what I'm trying to make. Juggernaut still gets used as well when I want more control over the image side.

ElevenLabs is probably the simplest one. I use it for character voices and system/voicemail stuff and it just saves a stupid amount of hassle, especially while lines are still changing.

And yes, the speed difference is massive. Codex especially. I simply couldn't build this at anything close to the same pace without it.

If I had to pay for only one thing, it would be Codex without much hesitation. ElevenLabs is also very easy for me to justify. Image generation is worth paying for too, but there I care less about one specific subscription because I constantly switch between models anyway.

Video is the one where I'm much more careful. The tools are great, but failed generations get expensive very quickly :D

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body:
Thanks for the answer. This is so interesting. 

“Missing” is not the sequel but happens in the same universe as “Searching”. It is not as good imo but there’s good ideas in there that maybe could inspire you further…  
A few more questions if you ever have time to answer.

Which Codex plan are you on, which models you use, for what, and what is your token burn like ?   
Are you able to let it run for a while within budget until the tasks are finished satisfactorily?  
How many hours did it take you to reach your current stage ? (It already looks very solid)  
Re Eleven Labs, can you give a bit more details on how you are using it? did you use voices in their catalog, custom voices; how much does it cost you, how long to customise?

Where will you release this when it’s done?

Anyway, solid work there. I’ll stay tuned.

replies.author: Kandoo85
replies.body:
Thanks :) And yeah, I’ll definitely check out Missing now. Searching is already pretty close to the general vibe I’m going for, so I’m curious what I can steal from it :D

For Codex I’m mostly using Astra Medium. That’s what I use for basically all the Unreal work.

Text-heavy stuff like dialogue, PDFs, documents etc. I either write myself if it’s important for the story, or I just use normal GPT. For that you really don’t need anything crazy, a normal Plus account would probably be enough. I mainly have Pro because of how much I use Codex.

So far I’d guess Codex itself has probably spent around 10–12 hours on the project. One time it absolutely destroyed my weekly limit though :D Now that the basic structure is there it’s a bit more relaxed.

If someone really wants to sit down and just crunch through a project for days, I’d probably go for the $200 plan. The $100 one is fine, but you can definitely hit the wall if you push it hard.

Overall I’ve probably spent around 20–30 hours on the game myself so far. I never tracked it properly though.

ElevenLabs is a bit of a special case for me. I already had the Pro plan for personal reasons, mainly because I use a voice clone of my wife after her illness. So I wouldn’t really use my subscription as an example for what you need for game dev :D I think it’s around $99/month, but you can do what I’m doing in the game much cheaper.

For the game I choose the voices manually. I already know what the characters look like and usually have a pretty clear idea of how I want them to sound, so I just go through voices until one feels right. Sometimes that takes 5 minutes, sometimes way longer.

Same with SFX. I do those myself as well. I don’t really let Codex decide any of that stuff.

Release-wise the plan is to get a proper Day 1 demo out first and see how people react.

The first full episode is also planned to be free.

The bigger idea is to make it as an anthology series. Different stories, different cases, but all somewhere around AI / ASI / AGI and the kind of things that can go wrong around that.

Searching is definitely one of the references, same with Black Mirror, and on the game side things like Orwell and Simulacra.

So the first episode is basically me proving to myself that the whole format actually works :D

If people enjoy it, I’d love to keep building more episodes around the same general universe.

And thanks again for the questions, really appreciate the interest :)

replies.author: Wooden_Plant7504
replies.body: Thanks for answering. Hope you crush it !
